I'm reading through this paper about myotonic dystrophy protein kinase, looking for the entities to annotate — the gene DMPK, the disease DM, and the mouse model experiments involving nullizygous and transgenic animals with altered DMPK expression levels.

The highest DMPK transgene expressers develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and higher neonatal mortality, but neither model reproduces the full DM phenotype — missing fibre-type atrophy, myotonia, cataracts, and male infertility — suggesting DMPK dosage alone isn't sufficient to cause the disease. I'm weighing whether "myopathy" in the title counts as a disease class term or something else, since it's framed as the outcome of abnormal DMPK levels.

Looking more closely, "myopathy" reads as a generic disease-family term, which leans toward Disease Class, though the "mild" severity modifier and the mouse-study context make it somewhat ambiguous whether it's naming a disease category versus describing a general pathological finding. I'll lean toward tagging "myopathy" as Disease Class.

Thinking about whether this matches the corpus style I recall, I'll settle on annotating "mild myopathy" as Disease Class per the manifestation-frame rule, since severity modifiers get included alongside the head term. Now moving to the next entity, "Myotonic dystrophy" itself, to decide its span and label.

For "Myotonic dystrophy (DM)" the full name is the clause's subject so it's Specific Disease, and the parenthetical "DM" also gets its own Specific Disease tag as an abbreviation. The causal phrase "CTG repeat expansions" isn't a disease mention, so I skip it. Then for "DM-protein kinase (DMPK)" — since the head noun denotes a protein, not a disease, the leading "DM" acts only as a hyphen-fused premodifier and should be tagged Modifier rather than a disease mention in its own right.

I continue applying that same Modifier tag to "DM" wherever it recurs as a premodifier in "DM-protein kinase," while leaving "DMPK" itself untagged since it's just the gene/protein abbreviation, not a disease reference. Other mentions like "Dmpk gene," "DMPK transgene," and "nullizygous mice" descriptions are gene/phenotype language, not disease mentions, so I pass over them too. Then I hit "hypertrophic cardiomyopathy" in the sentence about transgene expression — that's a genuine named disease appearing in a clause about what the animals showed, so that one needs a Specific Disease tag.

I also confirm "enhanced neonatal mortality" isn't a disease mention, just an outcome measure. For "other frequent DM symptoms," I'm treating "DM" there as an attributive premodifier of a non-disease head noun ("symptoms"), which under the negative-constraint rule for premodifiers of clinical heads doesn't get tagged as a disease mention on its own.

For the subsequent symptom list — "fibre-type dependent atrophy," "myotonia," "cataract," "male-infertility" — I need to check whether the "including" phrasing marks them as examples excluded from annotation or as standalone disease mentions.

Cataract and male-infertility both fit as Disease Class under the list rule, including the full premodified phrase "fibre-type dependent atrophy." Moving to "the disease" in the strengthening-contention sentence — this is anaphoric reference to DM already established, so it stays unannotated.

For the title, "myotonic dystrophy protein kinase" has "myotonic dystrophy" functioning as a Modifier premodifying "kinase," while "produce only mild myopathy in mice" gives me another Disease Class mention. Then in the next line, "Myotonic dystrophy (DM)" introduces the Specific Disease with its parenthetical abbreviation, and I'm noting how "DM" recurs both standalone and within "DM-protein kinase" as a Modifier, paralleling the abbreviation pattern for "DMPK."

I also consider "hypertrophic cardiomyopathy" — since it names a recognized specific condition rather than a general category, I classify it as Specific Disease even though it appears in a patient-presentation context. Now I'm working through the character offset counting for the annotation spans, carefully tracking each line and treating the newline as a single character to keep the indices accurate.

I'm computing exact character offsets for the key phrases "myotonic dystrophy" and "mild myopathy" on line one, then starting the same offset calculation for line two's text about CTG repeat expansions and DM-protein kinase.

Continuing to map out character positions through "DMPK" and into the sentence about altered expression levels of DMPK being ubiquitously expressed in all muscle cell lineages, examined by disrupting the gene.

I'm tracking position counts through the description of the knockout mice study, noting that nullizygous (-/-) mice showed only inconsistent and minor size changes in head and neck muscle fibres at older age.

Continuing to track character offsets through the passage, covering mentions of fibre-type dependent atrophy, myotonia, cataract, and male-infertility, then moving into the conclusion about these results strengthening the contention about simple loss- or gain-of-expression effects.

Now I'm working through the final sentence about DMPK not being the only crucial requirement for disease development, and I'm pausing to double-check my offsets by re-verifying the sentence about myotonic dystrophy, CTG repeat expansions, and DMPK expression levels in muscle cells against the original text.

Continuing the character-by-character count through "commonly associated with CTG repeat expansions within the gene for DM-protein kinase (DMPK), ubiquitously expressed in all..." to confirm each word lands on the expected position.

I'm now tracing through the discussion of how disrupting the endogenous Dmpk gene while overexpressing a human DMPK transgene in mice was used to study the effects of altered DMPK expression across muscle lineages during development, continuing the position count toward "Nullizygous" mice.

I'm counting through the description of nullizygous mice showing only inconsistent and minor size changes in head and neck muscle fibers at older age, while animals with the highest DMPK transgene expression showed hypertrophic effects, tracking character position as I go.

Continuing the character count through to the end of the sentence about strengthening the contention that simple loss- or gain-of-expression of DMPK isn't the only crucial requirement for disease development, landing at position 989. I want to double-check the earlier "endogenous" correction propagated consistently through this second counting pass before finalizing.

Now I'm verifying all the key annotation spans: "Myotonic dystrophy (DM)" as a Specific Disease with its parenthetical abbreviation, "DM" as a Modifier when fused to "protein kinase," "mild myopathy" and "hypertrophic cardiomyopathy" with their respective disease classifications, and the symptom list "fibre-type dependent atrophy, myotonia, cataract and male-infertility" each tagged as Disease Class.
